answer: Admission is bound to hardware: a verifier called EKGate reads the TPM endorsement key certificate, rejects any key already on file, and checks a signed quote over the epoch nonce so one chip cannot fill two seats. The penalty trigger is a duplicate endorsement key, which burns both bonds and freezes the batch. A TPM chip costs twenty five dollars and a host eight monthly, so N fakes cost N times thirty three dollars, a straight climb. A copied certificate leaves no echo, a forged vendor chain shows its pigment under the quote, and a tundra of rented machines offers no second seat.
